x: Matthew Cannon, having already reduced our Junior Boys record for 1500m by OVER HALF A MINUTE and added 24cm to the high jump mark, now added the 800 record to his tally - awe inspiring.

Neither of these lads can feel secure though because Peter Morris, running in their wake, has steadily chopped down his best to 5:03 and the outstanding Matthew Cannon has claimed the Colt's record with 4:59.

The outstanding Boy is John Fernee who won the Surrey Schools 400 metres and later finished 3rd in the Southern Boys 400 metres. In the Colts Matthew Cannon shows tremendous promise in all events. The enthusiasm of the young athletes is a joy to watch.

Several of the younger competitors managed to do the walk and the run and of these the most successful was Raymond McCann who won the former and still had enough left to get up to 5th over the same distance in the run, won convincingly by Matthew Cannon.
Whatever, Gerry Sexton, competing for Surrey, placed 22nd in the under 13 event whilst Matthew Cannon, in London's colours, came home 68th among the under 15's.
Mark Sinclair also closed right up on Alan. First colt to cross the finish line from a field of fifteen was Matthew Cannon in a very good time.
200 Metres · Matthew Cannon · Wimbledon Park · 14/7/76 · Hercules AC Trophy · 29.7
There were several other good performances, particularly Matthew Cannon's 800 metres run, but in this high standard competition the Bels had to be content with 5th team place.

Matthew Cannon, in his first year in the boys age group, set two new boys Club records to add to the six he already holds as a colt. He hurdled to a time of 12.7 seconds, reducing the old mark shared by Mark Shippen and John Fernee by three tenths, and also hacked over eight seconds off the 1500 met…

John Searle ran 5:04 and 5:05, Alan Perriam 5:07 and 5:00 but pride of place must go to 13 year old Matthew Cannon who confirmed that some of his reported timings at school were not way-out by running 5:03.
It was good to see how many of our boys and youths are progressing and special mention should be made of Mark Waller's, Matthew Cannon's David North's and John Searle's fine runs.

…fact that after our top two in most events, we have to struggle to find an adequate reserve. Eustace Aska, Dave Bailey, Matthew Cannon, Mick Manning etc. Where are you? - Now is the time to start getting ready for next season.…

In the October 1985 Edition of Running magazine regular columnist Geoffrey Cannon actually referred to the Belgravian and mentioned how in the past he enjoyed reading of the successes of his son Matthew. Many readers will remember Matt. Cannon who established several Club age group records in the mid 1970's.
